Absorbance that knows its wavelength and unit

Source: R/absorbance.R
absorbance.Rd

A chromr_absorbance vector holds absorbance values along with the wavelength they were measured at and their unit, AU or mAU. It is a double vector underneath, so it does arithmetic, compares and plots as numbers. The readers return it, so columns such as a280 keep their wavelength and unit when they are combined, and plots label their axes with the unit.

  • absorbance() creates absorbance values.

  • is_absorbance() tests whether an object is absorbance.

  • absorbance_wavelength() and absorbance_unit() give the wavelength in nm and the unit.

  • absorbance_convert() converts to another unit.

Combining absorbance in AU with absorbance in mAU, for example appending runs from different instruments, converts it to mAU. Combining absorbance at different wavelengths, as when pivoting to one column with pivot_wl_longer(), gives absorbance with no wavelength. Combining with plain numbers gives numbers.

Adding, subtracting, and scaling by numbers gives absorbance, so a baseline can be subtracted. Dividing absorbance by absorbance gives a plain ratio, such as A260/A280, after converting both to the same unit.

Usage

absorbance(x = double(), wavelength = NA, unit = c("mAU", "AU"))

is_absorbance(x)

absorbance_wavelength(x)

absorbance_unit(x)

absorbance_convert(x, unit = c("mAU", "AU"))

Arguments

x

For absorbance(), a numeric vector. For the other functions, an object to test, or absorbance.

wavelength

The wavelength in nm, or NA if it isn't known.

unit

The unit, "AU" or "mAU".

Value

absorbance() and absorbance_convert() return a chromr_absorbance vector. is_absorbance() returns a single logical. absorbance_wavelength() returns a number and absorbance_unit() a string.

Examples

x <- absorbance(c(0.1, 0.25), wavelength = 280, unit = "AU")
x
#> <absorbance<280 nm, AU>[2]>
#> [1] 0.10 0.25
absorbance_convert(x, "mAU")
#> <absorbance<280 nm, mAU>[2]>
#> [1] 100 250

# A260/A280 ratio
a260 <- absorbance(c(150, 400), wavelength = 260, unit = "mAU")
a260 / x
#> [1] 1.5 1.6

# Read from a file
fl <- system.file("extdata", "example_quadtec_3.txt", package = "chromr")
dat <- chrom_read_quadtech(fl)
absorbance_unit(dat$a280)
#> [1] "AU"
